# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->

R has some excellent tooling for code styling and linting, but there are gaps when thinking about consistency in the documentation and prose within R packages.
Hard-to-read documentation costs users time, puts off newcomers, and is becoming more common as more package code and documentation is written by AI tools.

Vale is the established tool for this job in many other ecosystems. It is a prose linter with rules defined as data, a library of published styles, and integrations for editors and CI.
It can read Markdown and pull the text out of comments in R files, but that is as far as its knowledge of R goes.
Its default styles report R function and argument names as spelling mistakes, it has no sense of how an R package is laid out, and it has to be installed and configured by hand outside of R.

This project fills that gap with an R package that installs and runs Vale, and a Vale style built for R packages.
Together they lint vignettes, READMEs and the comments in R source files, including the roxygen comments that become help pages, from the R console, the command line or a CI job.
The style is assembled from Vale's existing rules with thresholds set by running them across real CRAN packages and a vocabulary of R terms so the defaults are quiet out of the box.

The deliverables are the package on CRAN, the style published for anyone using Vale directly, and a GitHub Action, over two milestones ending in February 2027, for a total of $4,500.
